title: The 8 Levels of Instagram Story Envy
house: A bustling neon-lit metropolis made of organic markets, rooftop cafes, and subway tunnels, inhabited entirely by living fruit and vegetable people whose digital forehead displays broadcast their exact monthly net disposable income.
catchphrase: The number on your forehead never lies.
links: The barista at the Green Leaf Cafe mentions a quiet man in a tailored suit who always tips in fresh blueberries.
A discarded takeout bag from the downtown noodle joint appears in the background of three different stories.
The yellow subway line always smells faintly of overripe citrus during the morning rush hour.

levels.open_loop: What secret did Chloe's glowing story hide that made my entire phone freeze?

gegenspieler.tat: Laughs loudly at my frozen screen in the subway car and drops a designer iced latte cup on my shoe.

levels.name: Pip, 23, Barista
levels.story: The 8 levels of Instagram story envy. Level 1. Level 1: 1,200 dollars a month, and I am staring at my phone crying over a Mediterranean vacation story. I am Pip, 23, a tired little pear person working six days a week at the corner bean shop with a permanent coffee stain. I clicked on Chloe's story from high school. She is sunbathing on a yacht in Mykonos while my own rent is due tomorrow. Then I see the background of her video. Wait, is that my landlord sitting right next to her on that yacht drinking champagne? How is that even possible when he threatened to evict me yesterday for being two days late? You are staring at people who live in another universe while your own account is empty. I grit my teeth and grip my chipped ceramic mug tighter, my heart pounding against my pear skin. You'll see that in Level 2.

levels.name: Zesty, 25, Intern
levels.story: The 8 levels of Instagram story envy. Level 2. Level 2: 2,400 dollars a month – and my own lunchbox is mocking me in the office breakroom. I am Zesty, 25, a bright yellow lemon person trying to survive a brutal graphic design internship in downtown Seattle. I open Instagram and tap through my stories. There is Brad from high school posing next to a brand new electric sports car. Look at that poverty meal, get a real job. My skin turns extra sour and my juice starts to boil with pure humiliation after sixty hours of work this week. Then my phone buzzes violently against the Formica table with an unauthorized software invoice. You'll see that in Level 3.

levels.name: Brody, 29, Mechanic
levels.story: The 8 levels of Instagram story envy. Level 3. Level 3: 4,100 dollars a month – and my bank just bounced my garage rent payment for the second time. I am Brody, 29, a rugged broccoli stalk person covered in engine grease, working sixty hours under hydraulic lifts. I took a break to check Instagram stories and saw my former fraternity brother posting a VIP backstage pass. Your small business expansion loan has been formally denied. My stalks bristled with absolute rage as I looked at my own modest 4,100 dollar display glowing in the oily mirror. I built this shop with my bare hands while he inherited his dad's real estate firm. You'll see that in Level 4.

levels.name: Orange, 31, Realtor
levels.story: The 8 levels of Instagram story envy. Level 4. Level 4: 6,800 dollars a month – and the doorman just laughed in my face at the downtown rooftop lounge. I am Orange, 31, a round citrus person in a tailored charcoal suit trying to break into luxury real estate. I opened my Instagram story feed between client calls and saw my college rival posting champagne towers. You do not make enough to enter this section tonight. My citrus skin flushed bright orange with humiliation in front of the entire queue. I pay my taxes, I close deals, yet I am still treated like a peasant by people who inherit their portfolios. You'll see that in Level 5.

levels.name: Brooke, 34, Director
levels.story: The 8 levels of Instagram story envy. Level 5. Level 5: 9,500 dollars a month – and my own corporate presentation just turned into a public execution. I am Brooke, 34, a pristine broccoli person in a custom emerald blazer running marketing for a tech giant. I checked my Instagram stories before stepping onto the boardroom stage and saw my former intern posting vacation photos. As I clicked through my presentation slides, the projector suddenly flickered and flashed an old photo of me working at a deli. You used to chop lettuce for five bucks an hour, why pretend you belong here now? My green florets burned with intense humiliation while the executive board members whispered among themselves. You'll see that in Level 6.

levels.name: Dragon, 38, Investor
levels.story: The 8 levels of Instagram story envy. Level 6. Level 6: 12,800 dollars a month – and I just lost the penthouse of my dreams to someone with half my salary on their forehead. I am Dragon, 38, an exotic drachenfrucht person with vibrant pink and green skin, managing multi-million dollar tech portfolios. I was browsing Instagram stories during a private property viewing and saw my old real estate rival posting a victory selfie. I am sorry, Mr. Dragon, another buyer just wired double the deposit in cash five minutes ago. My pink dragon scales flushed with anger as I realized the person who outbid me was standing right behind the glass partition. He adjusted his charcoal suit and gave me a condescending nod while holding his sleek smartphone. You'll see that in Level 7.

levels.name: Sterling, 42, Executive
levels.story: The 8 levels of Instagram story envy. Level 7. Level 7: 14,200 dollars a month – and federal marshals just walked into my corner office with a warrant. I am Sterling, 42, a sleek eggplant person in a bespoke navy pinstripe suit running an international investment fund. I was reviewing Instagram stories on my tablet when my venture capital partner posted a live video celebrating a takeover. Your firm has been placed under emergency asset freeze due to an anonymous whistleblower report. My dark purple eggplant skin turned ghostly pale as federal marshals dropped a thick binder onto my desk. I looked out my window and saw my biggest competitor standing on the opposite rooftop holding his phone high. You'll see that in Level 8.

levels.name: Lord Coco, 50, Founder
levels.story: The 8 levels of Instagram story envy. Level 8. Level 8: 18,500 dollars a month – and I finally realize why every single person on this street hates the number on their forehead. I am Lord Coco, 50, a hard-shelled coconut person in a bespoke white linen suit who owns half the downtown skyline. I stood on my private rooftop terrace sipping champagne while watching Instagram stories of old classmates struggling below me. You think the number on your head makes you a god, but you are just renting space in everyone else's nightmare. My hard coconut shell cracked with sudden realization as I looked back at all the people I had stepped on. What theme should our city explore next in the comments?
